tracker-clip.mp4
  Two seconds of black: 320x240, 10 fps, 20 frames, no audio, 2 KB.
  Built with ffmpeg, not with OpenCV:

    ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "color=black:s=320x240:r=10:d=2" \
      -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 51 -g 20 \
      -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -an tests/fixtures/tracker-clip.mp4

  The test used to write this itself with cv2.VideoWriter and the "mp4v"
  fourcc. That codec is not in the OpenCV wheel for Intel macOS, so the file
  came out empty and reopened with zero frames - the test then failed on that
  runner alone, over a writer it never needed. A clip read from disk only asks
  the decoder, which every wheel has.
  Every frame is solid colour, so no subject is ever found: the tests that use
  this check the sampling and the size the decoder reports, not the tracking.
